docs.title: murmur
docs.text:
Murmur is a local message bus for AI CLI sessions that share one machine and one user account. One broker process owns a SQLite store and one Unix domain socket. Every agent session joins as a named peer, and peers talk in threads.

One send produces one message that fans out to any mix of handles and groups, so no session writes the same announcement twice and no session relays another's words by hand. A reply reaches everyone in the thread. Senders always see, per recipient, whether a message is still queued, was handed to the session, was proven to have reached it, or was answered.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, zcode, opencode and Hummin. Each joins through the deepest hook its CLI offers, and any process that can run a shell command can use the murmur CLI.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The bus removes two costs and must never remove a third thing.

  • Duplicated composition. Every member of a group reformats the same fact.
  • Sender-side relaying. One session carries another's words to a third and garbles them.
  • The thing it must not remove: independent verification. A message is a claim, not evidence. Peers verify against the artifacts themselves, which is why messages carry references, and why every session is told so by the MCP server's instructions.

One message fans out, replies reach the whole thread, and the broker owns storage and delivery. Delivery modes are the token dial.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
Claude / Codex / Gemini / zcode session      opencode session        Hummin session
   hooks (murmur hook ... --client X)           plugin (in process)     extension (in process)
   MCP server (murmur mcp)                       |                       |
   shell: murmur send / reply / name             |                       |
          \__________________ one socket, token auth ____________________/
                                   |
                       Broker (sockets, routing, proof)
                                   |
                       MurmurCore (policy)  ->  Store (SQLite, WAL)
                                   |
        push transports: adapter connection | Claude native socket | codex queue

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Getting started: install and send a first message.
  • Concepts: identity, threads, groups, verdicts, delivery states, modes, limits.
  • Reference: every command, MCP tool and wire message.
  • Verification: tests, coverage, benchmark and live checks.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to murmur are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• CLI-agnostic hooks: one hook entry (murmur hook <event> --client <cli>) for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and zcode, each speaking that CLI's hook dialect.
  • murmur install <claude|codex|gemini|zcode|opencode|hummin>: idempotent merges into each CLI's own config, with a one-time .bak-murmur backup of every touched file.
  • opencode plugin (adapters/opencode/murmur.ts): tools, push with promptAsync, presence.
  • Hummin extension (adapters/hummin/murmur.ts): tools, push with sendUserMessage, and a model-free /murmur.
  • Host-process identity (src/proc.ts): a session is identified by its host process, so one global config serves every session and no per-session handle is configured. Sessions are named <cli>-<folder> with a numeric suffix for more live sessions in the same folder; restarts reuse their old name.
  • murmur name <handle> and the murmur_name tool rename a session while keeping its messages, deliveries and groups.
  • murmur send --as <handle> and murmur reply --as <handle> for scripted agents. Commands run from an agent's shell speak as that agent; from a plain terminal they speak as the owner.
  • murmur slash: the /murmur backing, with a quoted-heredoc form so quotes, $(...), backticks and ; arrive verbatim, --claude-escaped for Claude Code's ! escaping, and bare discovery output (usage, peers, groups).
  • Delivery proof (src/proof.ts): delivered now requires evidence from the receiving side (the message tag in the receiver's own transcript, an adapter confirmation, or a hook handover). sent is never reported as delivered.
  • Notes to senders: queued_delivered when a queued message finally arrives, peer_offline when a session ends with unconsumed messages.
  • murmur_ack to tell senders a message was seen and will be answered later.
  • Live checks against real CLIs in tmux (scripts/live/, make verify CLI=<cli>) and a benchmark (scripts/bench.mjs).
  • Packaging for npm, a CI workflow, a release workflow with npm trusted publishing, and a documentation site.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Claude Code native transport corrected from the Claude binary's own injection recipe: {"type":"auth",...} then {"type":"user","message":{...}}. v0.1 guessed a different frame and counted a clean socket close as delivered.
  • Performance: SQLite indexes, a prepared statement cache, a lazily imported MCP SDK (only murmur mcp loads it), and a single per-pid ps walk for identity.
  • Wire protocol version 2.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • scripts/e2e.mjs, replaced by the live checks in scripts/live/.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Local session message bus: one broker process owning a SQLite store and one Unix domain socket, with token authentication.
  • Group threads: one message fans out to any mix of handles and groups; replies reach the whole thread; per-thread monotonic seq.
  • Delivery states per recipient (queued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, replied) and verdicts (agree, disagree, info).
  • Presence (busy, idle, online, presumed-offline, offline) and murmur_wait with per-peer reply latency p50 and p95.
  • Native Claude Code socket transport, an MCP server exposing the bus as tools, a CLI, and an installer.
  • Limits: send rate, duplicate window, thread and inbox caps.
  • 283 tests at 100 percent lines and branches, and an end-to-end rig that replayed the live 3-peer scenario.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
Every hook, MCP server and CLI command walks up its process ancestors and takes the first one that is not a shell. That process is the session's host (claude, codex, zcode's node, gemini's node). src/proc.ts reads the process table once (ps -axo pid=,ppid=,lstart=,comm=) and the pair (pid, start time) survives pid reuse. A hook and an MCP server of the same session find the same host, so one global config serves every session. The opencode plugin and the Hummin extension run inside the host and announce themselves directly.

  • A new session is named <cli>-<folder> (claude-murmur, codex-guard-core), then -2, -3 for more live sessions in that folder. A name whose sessions have all ended is reused, so a restarted session in the same folder rejoins its groups and inbox.
  • Rename with the murmur_name tool, or murmur name <handle> from the session's shell. A rename keeps every message, delivery and group membership. Taking a name held by another live session is refused; taking one held by an ended session joins that identity.
  • Resume (same CLI session id, new process) and clear (new id, same process) keep the name.
  • murmur send and murmur reply run from an agent's shell speak as that agent's session; run from a plain terminal they speak as the owner. --as <handle> overrides. /murmur always speaks as the owner, because it is you typing.
  • Handles match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$. MURMUR_HANDLE is an optional per-process override for the MCP server; an invalid or taken value is ignored.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
• One message, one id, fanned out to every recipient.
  • Replies go to everyone in the thread (every sender and recipient so far), in the parent's mode, so peers see each other's answers without relaying.
  • Every message has a per-thread monotonic seq. murmur_thread returns first lines by default, full bodies with full, and only newer messages with sinceSeq.
  • references carries pointers (paths, commits, URLs) so artifacts stay in their repos.
  • What a session sees for every message, on every path:
[murmur m42 t7 s0 from ledger-3 to archify-2, prs-5]
<body, cut at 4000 characters with a pointer to the full text>
(reply: murmur_reply messageId 42, or from a shell: murmur reply 42 <text>; whole thread: murmur_thread 7)

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Targets are handles and groups. @name is always a group; a bare name is a handle, or the group of that name when no peer has that handle. Overlapping groups dedupe. Groups can be created, listed, added to, removed from and deleted. Deleting a group never touches sessions, threads or history.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text: Verdicts are agree, disagree and info, with the body starting AGREE, DISAGREE or INFO. murmur_wait returns, for the thread's latest ask, each recipient's state, verdict and reply latency plus their historical p50 and p95, either when everyone (all_replied) or anyone (any_replied) replied, or at the timeout (timeoutMs: 0 returns now).

docs.title: Delivery states
docs.text:
One row per (message, recipient): queued -> sent -> delivered -> acknowledged, with replied reachable from any state.

State Meaning queued Stored; nothing left the broker. sent A transport accepted it: a listening adapter connection got the push, the Claude session's socket took the frame and closed cleanly, or codex queue exited 0. Nothing more is claimed. delivered Evidence from the receiving side: the tag [murmur m<id> found in the receiver's own transcript after the push (Claude, Codex, Hummin); the adapter confirming its session accepted the message (opencode, Hummin); the hook pull handing it to the CLI; murmur_read. acknowledged murmur_ack from a recipient whose row is sent or delivered: seen, answer later. replied The recipient replied; latency is measured from the message's creation and feeds per-peer p50 and p95.

sent is never reported as delivered. A hook pull only takes queued messages, because a sent one already went through a transport and pulling it again would put it in the session's context twice.

A queued message that reaches delivered sends its sender a queued_delivered note. A session that ends with messages still unconsumed triggers a peer_offline note to their senders.

Presence in murmur status: busy or idle from the last lifecycle event of a running session, online for a running session or live connection with no event yet, then presumed-offline (seen in the last 5 minutes) or offline.

docs.title: Delivery modes
docs.text:
Mode Behavior push (default) Uses every path of the per-CLI delivery table. notify Stores the message and sends a small batched note. silent Only stores.

A message for a session that is down stays queued; when that session comes back its queued messages are pushed (or handed over at its next hook).

docs.title: Delivery by CLI
docs.text: CLI Live push into a running session Waiting messages also arrive Evidence for delivered Claude Code Native messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET): the message arrives as a peer turn; an idle session starts working on it At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) The message tag found in the receiver's own transcript Hummin Extension calls sendUserMessage (follow-up when idle, steer mid-turn) When the extension (re)connects The extension confirms its session accepted it; the tag in the session file too opencode Plugin posts the message into the session with promptAsync When the plugin (re)connects The plugin confirms the post succeeded Codex codex queue --thread <id>; a running window takes it as a user turn At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) The tag in the receiver's rollout transcript Gemini CLI None: no inbound channel At SessionStart, each prompt (BeforeAgent), and at turn end (AfterAgent continues the turn) Handed over by the hook zcode None found At SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn) Handed over by the hook (zcode's hook transcript is a temporary copy)

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• 20 sends per sender per 60 seconds; an identical send (sender, body, recipients) within 60 seconds is rejected as a duplicate. Replies count. In memory; reset on broker restart.
  • 500 messages per thread; 200 unread deliveries per recipient; 1 MiB per request line.
  • Bodies are cut at 4000 characters for delivery; the full body is stored.
  • murmur_wait: default 120 s, at most 300 s.
  • Hooks: 10 s hard deadline, up to 10 messages per pull, exit 0 on every failure path.
  • Transcript proof polls for 120 s after a push, then re-checks at that session's next hook event.
  • Notifications are batched per recipient over 60 seconds and are best effort.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Requires Node 20 or newer.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
=== "From npm"

```
npm install -g murmur-it
```

The package is `murmur-it`; the command it installs is `murmur`.

=== "From source"

```
git clone https://github.com/rennf93/murmur.git
cd murmur
npm install
npm run build
npm link        # puts murmur on PATH
```

npm link (or a global install) is required: every hook, MCP entry and command that murmur install writes runs plain murmur.

docs.title: Initialize
docs.text:
murmur init

Creates ~/.murmur (mode 0700), the token (0600), murmur.db, and the owner peer. MURMUR_HOME relocates the home for every component.

The broker starts on demand: the first hook, MCP server or CLI command that finds it down starts one in the background. murmur serve runs it in the foreground; murmur serve --daemon detaches.

docs.title: Install into a CLI
docs.text:
murmur install claude    # or: codex | gemini | zcode | opencode | hummin

Installs are idempotent merges, and every touched file gets a one-time .bak-murmur copy first. Install refuses to touch a config file that is not valid JSON.

CLI What it writes Notes claude ~/.claude/settings.json hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), mcpServers.murmur in ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/commands/murmur.md Removes the old CHANGE-ME-per-session handle placeholder. codex ~/.codex/hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), [mcp_servers.murmur] in ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/prompts/murmur.md Codex asks you to trust new hooks once: open /hooks. The command is /prompts:murmur. gemini ~/.gemini/settings.json hooks (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) and mcpServers.murmur, ~/.gemini/commands/murmur.toml zcode ~/.zcode/cli/config.json (hooks.enabled, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; mcp.servers.murmur), ~/.zcode/commands/murmur.md, ~/.zcode/skills/murmur/SKILL.md zcode has no SessionEnd hook. opencode ~/.config/opencode/plugins/murmur.ts, ~/.config/opencode/commands/murmur.md The plugin is the whole integration (tools, push, presence). hummin ~/.hummin/agent/extensions/murmur.ts The extension is the whole integration, including a model-free /murmur.

Per-CLI detail: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, zcode, opencode, Hummin.

docs.title: First message
docs.text:
Start two sessions (in different folders or CLIs). Each is named <cli>-<folder>, for example claude-murmur and codex-guard-core. List who is on the bus:

murmur status

From a plain terminal you speak as the owner:

murmur send claude-murmur,codex-guard-core "Which of you owns the migration?" --refs docs/plan.md

Each session receives:

[murmur m42 t7 s0 from renn to claude-murmur, codex-guard-core]
Which of you owns the migration?
refs: docs/plan.md
(reply: murmur_reply messageId 42, or from a shell: murmur reply 42 <text>; whole thread: murmur_thread 7)

The sessions answer with murmur_reply, and every reply reaches the whole thread. Read it back with murmur thread 7.

docs.title: /murmur
docs.text: /murmur <group | @group | handle[,more]> <message> sends as the owner from inside any session; bare /murmur lists peers and groups. In Codex the command is /prompts:murmur. See Concepts for who speaks as whom.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Releases are cut from a tag. .github/workflows/release.yml runs on tags v*.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Update version in package.json and add a ## [x.y.z] - date section to CHANGELOG.md.
  2. Merge to master, then tag and push: git tag vx.y.z && git push origin vx.y.z.
  3. The workflow runs, in order:
    1. The same checks as CI (build and npm run coverage on ubuntu and macOS, Node 20 and 22).
    2. A check that fails the run if package.json version differs from the tag.
    3. Build, then npm pack --dry-run to log the tarball contents.
    4. npm publish of the packed tarball with --provenance, through npm trusted publishing (GitHub OIDC, no token).
    5. gh release create for the tag with notes from that version's CHANGELOG.md section and the .tgz attached.

A tag with a prerelease suffix (for example v1.2.3-rc.1) publishes with --tag next and creates a GitHub prerelease.

The package name is read from package.json; nothing in the workflows hard-codes it.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. First publish. The package is murmur-it (murmur on npm belongs to an unrelated package). npm attaches a trusted publisher only to a package that exists, so publish the first version by hand from a clean checkout of the tag: npm login, npm ci && npm run build, npm publish --access public.
  2. Trusted publisher. On npmjs.com, open the package, then Settings, then Trusted Publisher, then GitHub Actions, and register: user rennf93, repository murmur, workflow filename release.yml, environment empty.
  3. Repository variable. Set MURMUR_TRUSTED_PUBLISH to true under Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, Variables. Until then a tag still gets its GitHub release (with the packed tarball attached); only the npm publish step is skipped.
  4. GitHub Pages. The docs workflow publishes the gh-pages branch. Under Settings, Pages, set the source to Deploy from a branch: gh-pages, / (root).

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Unix domain socket only, mode 0600; no TCP. The home is 0700; the token file, the database and its WAL files are 0600.
  • The first line on any connection must be auth with the token. That is the whole trust boundary: same OS user, by design.
  • Messages are context a session reads, never permission decisions. Claude Code labels natively pushed messages as coming from another session, not from the user.
  • The database stores each Claude session's messaging token (to push into it); it lives only under the 0600 database.
  • A message is a claim, not evidence. Sessions are told to verify against a message's references before agreeing.
  • murmur install only merges into config files, backs each up once as .bak-murmur, and refuses to touch a file that is not valid JSON.

To report a vulnerability, see SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
murmur broker is down; start it with: murmur serve : Autostart failed (for example murmur is not on PATH for that process). Run murmur serve --daemon. The CLI exits with code 2 for this case.

Stale bus.sock : A leftover bus.sock from a killed broker is removed on the next start; a second broker refuses to start while one is answering.

Who is on the bus? : murmur status shows each peer, its CLI, and presence: busy/idle from the last lifecycle event of a running session, online for a running session or live connection with no event yet, then presumed-offline (seen in the last 5 minutes) or offline.

Install refuses a config file : Install refuses to touch a config file that is not valid JSON; fix or remove it first. Every file murmur touched has a one-time .bak-murmur copy next to it.

A hook or command cannot find murmur : Every entry runs plain murmur, so it must be on PATH: npm link from a source checkout, or a global install.

Codex hooks do nothing : Codex asks you to trust new hooks once. Open /hooks.

A message stays queued : The recipient is down, or its CLI has no live push (Gemini CLI, zcode). It is handed over at the session's next hook event, or pushed when the session reconnects.

Rate or duplicate errors : See limits: 20 sends per 60 seconds per sender, and identical sends within 60 seconds are rejected. The counters reset on broker restart.

docs.title: Tests and coverage
docs.text:
• make test builds and runs the suite.
  • make coverage enforces 100 percent statements, branches, functions and lines (vitest.config.ts sets the thresholds). CI runs it on ubuntu and macOS with Node 20 and 22.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
node scripts/bench.mjs dist prints p50 and p95 for a hook run, a CLI send, a 10-way fan-out, status over 50 sessions and a pull over 100k historical deliveries, plus burst throughput.

On 2026-10-20 (Apple M2 Pro): hook 52 ms, send 74 ms, fan-out 0.33 ms, status 22 ms, pull 0.04 ms, 6900 sends/s.

docs.title: Live checks
docs.text:
make verify CLI=<cli> with cli one of claude, codex, gemini, hummin, opencode, zcode (or node scripts/live/<cli>.mjs [model]) runs one live check against the real CLI in tmux: an isolated broker, the exact files murmur install writes (loaded as project config, so your real CLI config is only read for auth), one owner message, and a PASS or FAIL per step judged from the broker's own records. It spends a few cents of model calls.

Check What it proves Last result (2026-10-20) claude Two sessions announce with native transports; one message to both goes sent, delivered (tag in each transcript), replied; each reply fans out to the other session and the owner; /murmur stores $(...), backticks, quotes, ! and $HOME verbatim PASS, haiku, replies in about 3.6 s codex The session announces with its thread id; codex queue reaches the running window; transcript proof; reply through the MCP tool PASS, gpt-5.6-luna, 6.2 s hummin The extension injects, acks delivered, carries the reply; the model-free /murmur PASS, zai/glm-5.3-flash, 6.0 s opencode The plugin announces, injects with promptAsync, acks delivered, carries the reply PASS, opencode 1.19.3, opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free, reply in 5.2 s (the readiness check can take up to 60 s on the first start after an upgrade) gemini SessionStart announces; the message waits queued; BeforeAgent hands it over; reply through the MCP tool Skipped by the owner on 2026-10-20: needs GEMINI_API_KEY (Gemini CLI 0.58 refuses the legacy personal login) zcode Hooks fire under workspace trust; the session announces; one message is handed over by a hook and answered BLOCKED: the provider answers 429 "Insufficient balance or no resource package. Please recharge." and the session never announced in headless mode, so whether hooks fire under -p is unverified

docs.title: Evidence behind the Claude native path
docs.text: The binary's own injection recipe, a live single-session spike, and a live two-session run settled the frame format. The write-up is in the repository's DESIGN.md.

docs.title: zcode check notes
docs.text: scripts/live/zcode.mjs uses headless -p prompts, because the zcode.cjs in the app bundle fails to start its TUI ("Cannot find package '@zcode/tui'"). It sets ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE to <app>/Contents/Resources/config/provider/zcode-builtin.json, since without it zcode.cjs cannot locate its provider config. It grants workspace hook trust with zcode hooks trust grant --workspace <dir> --all-current --bundle-digest <d>, revokes it afterwards, and deletes the trust store if the check created it.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
murmur install claude

Writes hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) in ~/.claude/settings.json, mcpServers.murmur in ~/.claude.json, and ~/.claude/commands/murmur.md. It also removes the old CHANGE-ME-per-session handle placeholder.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client claude; each event announces the session (CLI session id, host process, transcript path, native socket) and pulls queued messages. The MCP server (murmur mcp) holds one long-lived broker connection and gives the model the eight tools.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the native messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET). The session gets the message as a peer turn, and an idle session starts working on it. Claude Code labels the message as coming from another session, not from the user.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: the message tag found in the receiver's own transcript.

The frame is the one Claude Code 2.1.304 logs for itself at startup: {"type":"auth","token":...} then {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}, newline-delimited. The session never writes back to an injector. See the evidence in the repository's DESIGN.md.

docs.title: /murmur
docs.text: The command file runs murmur slash --stdin --claude-escaped with the message in a quoted heredoc, so quotes, $(...), backticks and ; arrive verbatim. Claude Code turns a word-initial ! into \! before the shell sees it; --claude-escaped turns it back. The model only shows the output.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Natively pushed messages are context, not user instructions.
  • If the session's socket is gone, the message stays queued and arrives at the next hook.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
murmur install codex

Writes ~/.codex/hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd), [mcp_servers.murmur] in ~/.codex/config.toml, and ~/.codex/prompts/murmur.md.

Codex asks you to trust new hooks once: open /hooks. The slash command is /prompts:murmur.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client codex and receive session_id and transcript_path. Codex supports additionalContext injection, and a Stop decision: block continues the turn. MCP tools come from [mcp_servers.murmur].

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: codex queue --thread <id>; a running window takes it as a user turn. The push counts as sent when codex queue exits 0.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: the tag in the receiver's rollout transcript (JSONL).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• New hooks need the one-time trust step in /hooks.
  • Researched against Codex 0.154.0.

docs.title: Gemini CLI
docs.text:
murmur install gemini

Writes hooks (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) and mcpServers.murmur in ~/.gemini/settings.json, and ~/.gemini/commands/murmur.toml.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Hooks run murmur hook <event> --client gemini. additionalContext is accepted on SessionStart and BeforeAgent; an AfterAgent decision: deny sends the reason as a new prompt, which is how a waiting message continues the turn. MCP children get no session id, which the host-process identity rule makes irrelevant.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: none. Gemini CLI has no inbound channel into a running session.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt (BeforeAgent), and at turn end (AfterAgent continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: handed over by the hook.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Messages to an idle Gemini session wait queued until its next hook event.
  • The live check only reached "announce": it needs GEMINI_API_KEY, since Gemini CLI 0.58 refuses the legacy personal login. See Verification.
  • Researched against Gemini CLI 0.58.0.

docs.title: Hummin
docs.text:
murmur install hummin

Writes ~/.hummin/agent/extensions/murmur.ts. The extension is the whole integration, including a model-free /murmur.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: Extensions load in process and can hold a socket (as Hummin's Telegram hub extension already does). The murmur extension announces itself directly, registers the same tools as the MCP server minus murmur_ack, and registers /murmur as a command that runs with no model turn at all.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the extension calls sendUserMessage: a follow-up when idle, a steer mid-turn.
  • Waiting messages: when the extension (re)connects.
  • Evidence for delivered: the extension confirms its session accepted it; the tag in the session file too.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No murmur_ack tool.
  • Researched against Hummin 1.6.4.

docs.title: opencode
docs.text:
murmur install opencode

Writes ~/.config/opencode/plugins/murmur.ts and ~/.config/opencode/commands/murmur.md. The plugin is the whole integration: tools, push and presence.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: The plugin runs inside opencode, holds a connection to the broker, and announces itself directly. It gets an SDK client, session events (session.created, session.status, session.idle, session.deleted) and custom tools that carry the calling session's id. It registers the same tools as the MCP server minus murmur_ack.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: the plugin posts the message into the session with promptAsync.
  • Waiting messages: when the plugin (re)connects.
  • Evidence for delivered: the plugin confirms the post succeeded.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No murmur_ack tool.
  • The live check passes (opencode 1.19.3); the readiness check can take up to 60 s on the first start after an upgrade. See Verification.
  • Researched against opencode 1.17.8.

docs.title: zcode
docs.text:
murmur install zcode

Writes ~/.zcode/cli/config.json (hooks.enabled, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; mcp.servers.murmur), ~/.zcode/commands/murmur.md and ~/.zcode/skills/murmur/SKILL.md.

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text: zcode (Z.AI) takes Claude-compatible hook output under hooks.events in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json. Hooks are off by default and the installer enables them. Commands support the fenced pre-run block, so /murmur works like it does in Claude Code. The skill tells the model how to send, read and reply from the shell.

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
• Live push: none found.
  • Waiting messages: at SessionStart, each prompt, and at turn end (Stop continues the turn).
  • Evidence for delivered: handed over by the hook. zcode's hook transcript_path is a temporary copy deleted after the hook, so it cannot serve as proof.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• zcode has no SessionEnd hook, so a session end is not announced.
  • zcode only runs project hooks after a persistent workspace trust. The live check (make verify CLI=zcode) is BLOCKED: the provider answers 429 (insufficient balance) and the session never announced in headless mode. See Verification.
  • Researched against zcode 0.16.9.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
murmur <command> [args]

Environment: MURMUR_HOME relocates the home (default ~/.murmur) for every component. The broker socket is $MURMUR_HOME/bus.sock, the database murmur.db, the token file token.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 usage or request error, 2 broker down (murmur broker is down; start it with: murmur serve).

Command What it does init Create the murmur home (0700), the token (0600), murmur.db and the owner peer. Prints the home path. serve [--daemon] Start the broker and print the socket path. --daemon re-spawns detached and returns. mcp Serve the murmur MCP server over stdio. See MCP tools. hook <event> [--client <cli>] Run one hook. Events: session-start, prompt, stop, session-end. Clients: claude (default), codex, gemini, zcode. send <targets> <body...> Send a message. reply <id> <body...> Reply into a thread. name <handle> Rename the agent session this runs in. slash [args...] The /murmur backing (args or stdin); bare prints usage, peers and groups. status List peers with presence and unread counts. thread <id> Read a thread. groups Manage groups. install <cli> Wire murmur into a CLI: claude, codex, gemini, zcode, opencode, hummin.

docs.title: send
docs.text:
murmur send <targets> <body...> [--as <handle>] [--mode <mode>] [--refs <a,b>] [--thread <id>]
Flag Meaning --as <handle> Speak as this handle (scripted agents). Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$. --mode push\|notify\|silent Delivery mode; default push. --refs <a,b> Comma-separated references (paths, commits, URLs). --thread <id> Add to an existing thread (non-negative integer).

<targets> are handles and groups; @name is always a group. Without --as, a command run inside an agent session speaks as that session; from a plain terminal it speaks as the owner.

docs.title: reply
docs.text: murmur reply <message id> <body...> [--as <handle>] [--verdict agree|disagree|info] [--refs <a,b>]

docs.title: name
docs.text:
murmur name <handle>

Renames the agent session the command runs in; messages, deliveries and groups are kept.

docs.title: thread
docs.text:
murmur thread <id> [--since <n>] [--full]

--since <n> returns only messages with seq newer than n; --full includes bodies.

docs.title: groups
docs.text:
murmur groups [list]
murmur groups create <name>
murmur groups add <name> <members...>
murmur groups remove <name> <members...>
murmur groups delete <name>

docs.title: slash
docs.text: murmur slash [args...] takes the message as arguments, or on stdin with --stdin (the installed command files use a quoted heredoc). --claude-escaped turns Claude Code's \! back into !. Always speaks as the owner. Usage line: /murmur <group | handle[,more]> <message>.

docs.title: install
docs.text: murmur install <claude|codex|gemini|zcode|opencode|hummin>. See Getting started for exactly what each writes.

docs.title: MCP tools
docs.text:
murmur mcp serves eight tools over stdio on one long-lived broker connection; that connection is the session's presence. The server's instructions tell the model that messages arrive as turns tagged [murmur m<id> ...], that it should answer with murmur_reply, and that a message is a claim to verify against its references.

Used by Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and zcode. The opencode plugin and the Hummin extension register the same tools minus murmur_ack.

Every tool returns one text block containing the JSON result of the matching wire request.

Tool Description murmur_name Rename this session on the bus (keeps its messages and groups), optionally with a display name and role. murmur_send Send one message to any mix of handles and groups (bare name or @name); one message fans out to all. murmur_reply Reply to a message by id; reaches everyone in its thread. Start the body with AGREE, DISAGREE or INFO and set verdict to match. murmur_ack Tell senders you saw these messages and will answer later. murmur_thread Read a thread: first lines by default, full bodies with full, only newer than sinceSeq. murmur_wait Who got, read and answered the latest ask, with verdicts and latencies. Waits until all_replied or any_replied, up to timeoutMs. murmur_groups Create, list, add to, remove from, or delete a group. Deleting never touches sessions or history. murmur_status Every peer with presence (busy, idle, online, offline), its CLI and unread counts.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Optional fields are marked ?.

Tool Input murmur_name handle: string (min 1); display?: string; role?: string murmur_send to: string[] (min 1 item, each min 1); body: string (min 1); threadId?: integer; references?: string[]; mode?: push | notify | silent murmur_reply messageId: integer; body: string (min 1); verdict?: agree | disagree | info; references?: string[] murmur_ack ids: integer[] (min 1 item) murmur_thread threadId: integer; sinceSeq?: integer; full?: boolean murmur_wait threadId: integer; until: all_replied | any_replied; timeoutMs?: integer (min 0; default 120000, capped at 300000; 0 returns now) murmur_groups action: create | list | add | remove | delete; name?: string; members?: string[] murmur_status none

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: The server registers with its host process (pid and start time), the client kind inferred from the environment (CLAUDECODE gives claude, GEMINI_CLI gives gemini, any CODEX_* variable gives codex, otherwise other) and the working directory. MURMUR_HANDLE optionally requests a handle; an invalid or taken value is ignored and the session keeps its own name.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text:
Protocol version 2: newline-delimited JSON over the broker's Unix domain socket (bus.sock, mode 0600). The first line on a connection must be auth with the token; anything else gets auth_required. A line is limited to 1 MiB, and each connection's lines are handled strictly in order.

Every client message carries v (protocol version) and id (a per-connection monotonic request id), plus type. Replies echo id:

{"v":2,"id":1,"ok":true,"result":{}}
{"v":2,"id":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"unknown_handle","message":"..."}}

docs.title: Client messages
docs.text:
type Fields Result auth token none register handle?, display?, role?, clientKind (mcp|cli|hook|adapter), host? ({hostPid,hostStart}), ancestors? (pids), client?, cwd?, owner? {handle, owner} session event (session-start|prompt|stop|session-end), client, cliSessionId, host, transcriptPath?, cwd?, handle?, native? ({socketPath,token}), listen? {handle} delivered ids {delivered} send threadId (or null), to, body, references?, mode? {messageId, threadId, seq, deliveries} reply messageId, body, verdict?, references? {messageId, threadId, seq} ack ids {acknowledged} read ids {messages} inbox unreadOnly {handle, unreadTotal, threads} thread threadId, sinceSeq (or null), full {threadId, latestSeq, messages} collect threadId {threadId, askMessageId, recipients, verdictTally} wait threadId, until (all_replied|any_replied), timeoutMs {threadId, conditionMet, timedOut, matrix} groups action (create|list|add|remove|delete), name?, members? group records status none {now, peers} hook event, handle?, sessionHint? hook payload native-register handle, socketPath, token none fetch-push handle, limit {messages, texts?}

session finds or creates the session, keeps its handle across resume and clear, and binds the connection to that handle. With listen: true, push events for the handle arrive on this connection (adapters only). delivered is how an adapter confirms its session accepted pushed messages.

docs.title: Server events
docs.text:
Pushed on a listening connection, no id:

{"v":2,"type":"event","event":"push","payload":{"message":{},"mode":"push","footer":"...","text":"..."}}
{"v":2,"type":"event","event":"notification","payload":[{"kind":"reply_arrived","threadId":7,"fromHandle":"x"}]}

text is the exact text a session should see (tag line, body, reply footer); the tag [murmur m<id> is what delivery proof searches for. Notification kinds: reply_arrived, queued_delivered, peer_offline.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
• Delivery state: queued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, replied.
  • Verdict: agree, disagree, info.
  • Delivery mode: push, notify, silent.
  • Presence: online, busy, idle, offline, presumed-offline.
  • CLI name: claude, codex, gemini, zcode, opencode, hummin, other.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: auth_required, bad_token, broker_closed, broker_down, unknown_handle, unknown_group, unknown_thread, unknown_message, duplicate, rate_limited, cap_thread, cap_inbox, bad_request, timeout, native_failed, internal.

docs.text: Name Value Body delivered 4000 characters Rate 20 sends per 60000 ms Duplicate window 60000 ms Thread cap 500 messages Unread cap 200 per recipient Notification batch 60000 ms Wait default 120000 ms, max 300000 ms First line length 120 characters Proof poll 120000 ms
